# Patient eXperience Consulting (PXC)

> PXC fixes the front desk at independent medical practices. We find the three front-desk problems driving the rest, fix them with the practice's own team in 90 days, and measure the result on the same sheet we started with. One offer: the 90-Day Medical Front Desk Reset.

## Facts

- Who it is for: independent medical practices with 2 to 20 providers and one or two locations.
- Founder: Jennifer Radu, C.P.P.M. 21 years running medical practices, including 12 urgent care clinics across four counties at once. Former teacher.
- Location: Bradenton, FL. All work is virtual, nationwide.
- Phone: (941) 239-2309
- Patient information: never requested, never collected.

## The offer, in three steps

- Free Front Desk Screener, $0: ten questions, about five minutes, a first read on where the friction starts, and a 20-minute review call.
- Practice Audit, $1,500: a five-day count with no patient information, an observation of the hardest hour, findings, and an agreed Top 3. Credited to the Reset if the practice signs within 30 days of the findings call.
- 90-Day Medical Front Desk Reset, $12,500 for one location (half at signing, half at kickoff; additional locations $3,000 each): three priorities fixed with the team, each with a written rule, a named owner, a script, training and a weekly number. AI tools are set up only where the audit shows they fit.

## The Keep-Working Promise

If the day-90 measure is missed and the practice met its side of the plan, PXC keeps working on the same three priorities at no added fee, through day 180. It is not a refund, and results are not guaranteed.

## The ten front desk dominoes

1. Phones and Callbacks: A missed call with no owner is still open at the end of the day, and the patient calls again.
2. Arrival and Check-In: Forms, insurance questions and a line at the window all start at the same minute.
3. Wait Time and Flow: A delay nobody names feels longer, and the desk absorbs the frustration.
4. Scheduling Integrity: Overrides with no rule fill the day past what the team can actually run.
5. No-Shows and Confirmations: A reminder goes out, nobody owns the reply, and an open slot sits empty.
6. Checkout and Follow-Through: The visit ends at the door, and the next step is nobody's task.
7. Admin Requests and Messages: Refills, forms, records and portal notes share one pile and no turnaround.
8. Handoffs and Escalation: Front-to-clinical handoffs depend on who happens to be nearby.
9. Team Stability and Onboarding: A new hire inherits whatever was never written down, and the pattern repeats.
10. Reputation and Feedback: Reviews are often the last domino. Nine others fell first.

## Common questions

- What does PXC actually do? We fix front-desk operations at independent medical practices. We find the three problems causing the most trouble, fix them with your team over 90 days, and measure the result.
- Is the free screener an audit? No. The screener is ten questions and a first read. The Practice Audit is a five-day count and observation.
- How much does the 90-Day Reset cost? $12,500 for one location, half at signing and half at kickoff. The $1,500 audit is credited if you sign within 30 days.
- Do we have to buy AI? No. AI is set up only where your audit shows it will help your team.
- Will you need patient records? No. We never ask for patient information.
- What happens after day 90? Your team keeps the huddle, the scoreboard and the monthly review. If the day-90 number was missed and you met your side, we keep working through day 180.
- Who is this for? Independent practices with 2 to 20 providers and one or two locations.
- Do you come on-site? All work is virtual, nationwide, from Bradenton, Florida.
